claims.exact_statement: For a fixed pseudoknot-free target structure, stipulated nearest-neighbor energy model, and allowed sequence set, the optimization problem of maximizing target Boltzmann probability or minimizing normalized ensemble defect is already directly addressed by published RNA design methods; SamplingDesign explicitly supports arbitrary per-sequence objectives and evaluates these ensemble objectives.
assumptions: The proposed task supplies a target secondary structure and a fixed folding-energy model.
The objective is target Boltzmann probability or normalized ensemble defect.
The novelty being considered is the generic sequence-search formulation, not a new guarantee or experimental result.
claims.status: primary-literature-supported principled rejection of generic novelty; no new theorem claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: Does not rule out a new algorithm with a materially different objective, rigorous guarantee, kinetic interface, or experimentally demonstrated advantage. No global-optimality, physical-model accuracy, or biological-performance claim follows from published in-silico benchmarks.

costs.inputs: Target structure, sequence constraints, temperature/solution condition, and fixed thermodynamic parameters are supplied.
costs.runtime: Published SamplingDesign uses Monte Carlo objective/gradient samples, reports 2500 samples per update in its configuration, and reevaluates final candidates in ViennaRNA v2.6.4. Each exact pseudoknot-free partition-function evaluation has cubic sequence-length cost under the standard dynamic program; total work scales with sampled candidates, conditions, and optimization updates.
costs.experimental: Sequence synthesis, model calibration, cotranscriptional trajectory acquisition, chemical probing, and reporter validation are not included in the in-silico benchmark cost.

claims.falsifier: A demonstration that the inspected method does not in fact evaluate these exact target-probability/NED objectives would falsify the stated subsumption; a genuinely distinct objective or guarantee with an equally informed benchmark or experiment would falsify the broader decision to reject a differentiated claim.
claims.next_gate: Freeze a measurable multi-condition cotranscriptional occupancy/readthrough objective and compare a new optimizer against SamplingDesign with the same objective when applicable, SAMFEO, local/constraint-based search, and a trajectory-fitted kinetic baseline under equal model inputs, sequence count, evaluator calls, and wet-lab budget.

claims.exact_statement: Target occupancy alone does not determine the full distribution of off-target RNA conformations or any observable that distinguishes those off-targets.
assumptions: The structure set contains at least one target and two distinct off-target states.
The assay output may depend differently on the two off-target states.
claims.status: internally verified exact finite counterexample; elementary and not a novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Only distinguishes scalar target occupancy from full-distribution control. It does not challenge published ensemble-objective optimizers or establish a biological example.

costs.inputs: Three abstract structure/macrostates and an output map are specified.

claims.falsifier: A derivation showing that equal target occupancy forces equal probability of every off-target state under the stated three-state setup.
claims.next_gate: Use a task-specific macrostate partition and assay readout before claiming distribution control.

claims.exact_statement: The inspected primary sources establish cotranscriptional RNA population/pathway predictors and equilibrium ensemble sequence optimizers, but this bounded audit did not establish a validated, generally novel algorithm that optimizes sequence for experimentally measured multi-condition cotranscriptional response under rate and energy uncertainty.
assumptions: The question is sequence optimization for measured kinetic response across ligand, transcription, or pause conditions.
The bounded primary-source search and supplied biomolecular reports define the audited scope.
claims.status: UNKNOWN; open research direction, novelty and capability unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: Not a claim that no such method exists. No new kinetic design algorithm was implemented or tested here.

costs.inputs: Would require a defined target response over time/ligand/pause schedules, a kinetic state model or direct trajectory evaluator, and frozen sequence-edit constraints.
costs.runtime: Not measured; kinetic simulation and repeated sequence/condition evaluations dominate until specified.
costs.experimental: Would require sequence synthesis/QC, state-resolved trajectories or cotranscriptional probing, reporters, and held-out-condition assays; none was acquired.

claims.falsifier: A primary-source algorithm demonstrably covers the exact prespecified kinetic sequence-optimization interface; this would close the proposed gap. Conversely, a matched held-out assay showing better calibrated response per total budget could support a candidate advance after an expanded novelty search.
claims.next_gate: Define the kinetic response vector, acquire or calibrate rates, implement the common evaluator, compare equally informed baselines, then prospectively validate held-out constructs and transcription conditions.
